judgments.reasoning_cat1: The carve-outs are the classic battleground: 'any unpaid, unrecoverable or outstanding loan, lease or extension of credit to any customer', 'restitution, disgorgement, or payment of similar sums' and 'matters which are uninsurable under the law' are each capable of a narrow or a sweeping reading, and the loan carve-out could swallow the very damages a failed-bank claim seeks.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against the Insuring Agreements (c032–c034), which promise to pay what Insured Persons are 'legally obligated to pay', an expansive reading of carve-out (3) would gut the principal coverage; the Fiduciary endorsement (c153) also substitutes a differently worded Loss definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short administrative definition; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used only in Section XVI(H) (c119), consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'first named entity set forth of Item 1' contains a small grammatical slip but the sense is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The name-change endorsement (c025) reordered Item 1 so that Vantus Bank became first-named, silently shifting who is Named Insured for cancellation (c104) and authorization (c115).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Simple compendium definition of the Policy documents.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the Declarations' contract-constitution sentence (c018) and the entire-agreement clause (c113).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite by reference to Item 2, with 'or any earlier termination date' a clear tailpiece.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Change Policy Period endorsement (c020) and the Discovery Activation termination date (c002) both operate on this definition without contradicting it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The deeming rule for extensions is convoluted but self-consistent; the terms are precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The one-month extension in c020 and the Discovery Period deeming rule in c037 both fold into this Policy Year concept, which controls whether a fresh limit is available.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'include but are not limited to' followed by a list makes the outer reach of Pollutants genuinely open-ended, and 'thermal organism' is a garbled phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds only the Pollution exclusion (c073) and does not clash with any other provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two-limb definition tied to registration or licensing; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used only in the Brokerage/Advisory Services definition (c039); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is scrambled in transcription and the ownership thresholds are inconsistent between limbs ('more than fifty percent' versus 'fifty percent or more'), a drafting mismatch.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subsidiary drives the Company definition (c042), the Subsidiary exclusion (c077) and the Conversion clause (c106), all of which turn on percentage thresholds.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long enumerated list closing with 'trustee exercising any other trust or fiduciary powers permitted by law', a catch-all whose reach against the specifics is uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defines the scope of the Trust Department Services exclusion (c078) and interacts with the Wrongful Act IRA/Keogh limb (c061(2)), which carves out trust department activity.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'while acting solely in the capacity as such' is a recurring source of dispute over dual-capacity conduct, and limb (3) is circular in tying Wrongful Acts of the Company to the grant of coverage.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Limb (2) refers to IRA/Keogh acts 'outside of the scope of any Trust Department', which must be squared with Item 11's retention and the Section VII(A)(4) reinstatement keyed to Section IV(X)(2).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line applicability statement; plainly worded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Three endorsements (c131, c154, c168) selectively disapply parts of Section V, so 'applicable to all Insureds under all Insuring Agreements' is qualified elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long specific list of injury torts; broad but each item is named, and 'intangible property' is the only soft edge.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No competing provision grants such coverage, so it fits the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'arising out of or in any way involving' is broad but standard, and it points to a defined service.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Brokerage endorsement (c131) deletes this very exclusion for that coverage, an interaction that is expressly handled but must be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'totally without the solicitation, assistance, participation, or intervention of any Insured' is a demanding and imprecise standard to apply in practice.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It largely duplicates limb (3) of the Insured vs. Insured exclusion (c072), so the two must be read consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The enumerated employment wrongs are followed by 'any other violation of any statutory or common law relating to employment', a catch-all whose reach against the specifics is contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with the ERISA exclusion (c067) and the Fiduciary endorsement's employment-law exclusion (c160) but does not contradict them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Very wide ('in any way involving any pension, profit sharing or employee benefit program'), but each element is named.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is deleted for fiduciary coverage by c154, which is exactly how the endorsement is meant to work.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The carve-back for 'the foreclosure process' and one-to-four family property is a specific exception whose boundary against the broad exclusion could be argued.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision addresses foreclosed property, so it stands alone coherently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final-adjudication proviso plus the 'other than Defense Costs' opening make the trigger reasonably clear, though 'arising out of or in any way involving' is broad.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The parallel Illegal Profit exclusion (c070) uses 'in fact' with no final-adjudication requirement, and Section XV(C) imputes officer knowledge to the Company for exclusions (G) and (H) alike.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'involving, in fact' is an odd, under-specified trigger and limb (3) ('conflicts of interest, engaging in self-dealing, or acting in bad faith') is vague enough to swallow ordinary negligence claims.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against the Fraud exclusion (c069), which requires a final adjudication for a comparable set of conduct, leaving the two triggers hard to reconcile.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad 'in any way involving' language with a defined term and a narrow parenthetical exception; workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The parenthetical matches the corresponding carve-out in the Brokerage/Advisory Services definition (c039), so the instrument is consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Whether a claim by a statutory receiver standing in the institution's shoes is a Claim 'by, on behalf of, or at the behest of the Company' is the paradigm lexical dispute, and the three enumerated exceptions invite an expressio unius argument that no other claimant escapes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Policy elsewhere expressly contemplates receivership — Financial Impairment (c046), the Insolvency/Bankruptcy clause (c120) preserving the Insurer's obligations, the Conversion clause (c106) and the zero-retention rule (c091) — so applying the exclusion to a receiver's claim arguably leaves the instrument incoherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard two-limb pollution wording resting on the open-ended Pollutants definition, with a tailpiece extending it to claims alleging damage to the Company.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with the Pollutants definition (c057) and conflicts with nothing else in the Policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Reaches any 'fact, circumstance or situation' noticed to another carrier — very broad, and it turns on the elastic Interrelated Wrongful Acts concept.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It complements Section X(B) notice (c098) and the Other Insurance clause (c118), but the two notice regimes must be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The garbled verb ('shall m4 liable') is scanning noise; 'the same or substantially the same fact, circumstance or situation' is a soft but familiar test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on the Item 12 prior/pending dates, which are supplied for the live coverages, so no gap appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Tied to a specific statute and a defined transaction type; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No competing provision; it fits the securities coverage scheme.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It closes with an exception 'except as provided in Section XII (C)(3)', but Section XII(C) has only two subparts — a cross-reference to a provision that does not exist.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Worse, Section XII is replaced by the Mergers endorsement and deleted outright by the Discovery Activation endorsement (c006), so the saving exception has no ascertainable content.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short exclusion resting on a defined term; nothing ambiguous of its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It squares with the Wrongful Act limb (2), which covers IRA/Keogh activity only outside the Trust Department.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line applicability statement; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section VI applies only to Agreement (C), while several of its exclusions are re-added by endorsement for other coverages — parallel rather than conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'directly or indirectly by or for the benefit of any insurance carrier' is broad but the class of claimants is named.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Repeated verbatim in three endorsements (c132, c156, c169) with no variation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 'unless such liability would be imposed regardless of the existence of such contract' proviso is a familiar but fact-sensitive carve-back.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with Loss carve-out (5) in c051, which addresses contractual obligations differently; the two need reading together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and specific to fee disputes; little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates Loss carve-out (7) in c051, consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (1) excludes claims 'in any way involving the Financial Impairment of the Company', which is extremely broad given the defined term's receivership trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That sits in real tension with Section XVI(I) (c120), which says Financial Impairment shall not release the Insurer, with the zero-retention rule in c091(1)(b) and with the Order of Payments clause (c094(3)).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three enumerated service categories closing with 'or provider of like services', a modest catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Repeated in the Brokerage endorsement (c136); no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list ends with 'any other investment banking activity', a general catch-all following specifics that invites an ejusdem generis fight, and limb (5) sweeps in any acquisition or sale of Company securities for its own account.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its breadth rubs against the Securities Liability Insuring Agreement (c165), which covers claims involving the purchase or sale of securities issued by the Company, and the same exclusion is re-added there (c173).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Turns on an objectively ascertainable legal lending limit at the time of the extension of credit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with the Loss carve-out for unpaid loans (c051(3)) without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A specific physical-appearance condition; clear enough to apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision addresses notarial acts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the Company's function or activity as receiver' is directed at the Company acting as receiver, but the label 'Receivership Exclusion' could be read as reaching claims by a receiver.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Any such broader reading would collide with Financial Impairment (c046) and Section XVI(I) (c120), which assume coverage survives a receivership.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Narrow and specific to safe deposit operations.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No competing provision in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Dense but arithmetically precise; subpart (2)'s reference to 'the D&O Limit of Liability set forth in Item 8' is loose, since Item 8 lists several limits.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be reconciled with Item 3's total policy limit (c011), the non-erosion clause (c093) and the reinstatements in c090(4) and c161, which together create a complicated but arguably consistent limit structure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 'not permitted or required by law to advance ... or indemnify' test and 'solely by reason of its Financial Impairment' are contestable triggers with real money attached.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Discovery Period endorsement (c004) states a differently worded retention rule for an acquiring entity, and Section VIII(A)(2) (c093) deems such Loss paid under Agreement (B).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Aggregation hinges on the elastic 'Interrelated Wrongful Acts' concept, and relation-back to a Claim first made before the Policy Period is a standard flashpoint.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with the definition in c050 and the Discovery Period deeming rule in c037, whose relation-back rules must be reconciled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conditioned on whether a limit is a 'sublimit of the D&O Policy' or separate under Item 7 — a distinction the Declarations record only by an 'X' column left blank.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes Item 7 entries that do not exist in the Declarations table, so its operation depends on reading the table (c014) as making every limit a sublimit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'in the Insurer's judgment could reasonably exceed' hands the trigger to the Insurer, but the sequence of payments is stated clearly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the non-erosion clause (c093) and the Insolvency/Bankruptcy provision (c120).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'mutually agreed upon' counsel and consent 'not unreasonably withheld' are soft standards, but they are conventional and paired with a reasonableness qualifier.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits with the advancement obligation (c096) and the arbitration mechanism (c108), which together handle disputed defense spending.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The advancement duty is clear, and the repayment obligation is expressly conditioned on it being 'established' that there is no liability.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is subject to Section XIV and dovetails with the arbitration and allocation rules (c107, c108).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It combines an elastic 'as soon as practicable' with a hard sixty-day outer limit, a pairing that can be read as two different standards.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The interplay with Section X(B) potential-claim notice (c098) and the Discovery Period's bar on circumstance notices (c037) is where late-notice fights arise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The specificity demanded ('full particulars as to the names, dates and persons ... the identity of the potential plaintiffs and the causes of action') is a condition precedent whose sufficiency is inherently arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section III (c037) expressly forbids such notice during the Discovery Period, which matters when a Policy has already terminated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pointer to Item 5 with a scanning gap in the middle of the sentence; the sense is obvious.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Declarations Item 5 (c013).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'all information reasonably requested' is qualified by reasonableness, a familiar and applicable standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reinforces the condition-precedent structure of Section X and Section XVI(F); no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The consent machinery is clear, though 'any transaction or event' in the coverage cut-off is unusually wide.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This subsection is deleted and replaced by the Mergers endorsement (c179), which uses a 20% threshold rather than 25%, and Section XII is then deleted entirely by c006.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clean automatic-coverage rule keyed to a percentage of assets.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is superseded by c180 (20% threshold) and then removed altogether by the Discovery Activation deletion of Section XII (c006), leaving three versions in the record.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Very broad ('directly or indirectly resulting from') and its final clause trails off without a closing, a mechanical flaw.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It survives the Mergers endorsement, which replaces only (A) and (B), yet the Discovery endorsement deletes all of Section XII — so whether (C) still operates is genuinely unclear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Precise percentages and a clear pre/post-anniversary distinction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits alongside the Insurer cancellation return of 100% (c105) and the noncancellable Discovery Period (c007) without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed notice mechanics with specific day counts; little room for two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subsection (B)(1) is deleted and replaced by the Iowa Amendatory Endorsement (c187), which substitutes a different and longer set of cancellation grounds.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The conversion triggers are enumerated, but 'ceasing to engage actively in its primary business' is a vague test and the run-off effect ('coverage shall cease with respect to Claims for such Wrongful Acts committed ... after such event') is awkwardly phrased.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It preserves the Discovery Period right under Section III, yet Section III only allows Discovery on conversion 'subject to Section XIII (C)(1)(b)', a narrower cross-reference than (C)(1) as a whole.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'relative legal exposures of the parties' is an inherently indeterminate allocation standard, and the 100% presumption in (1)(a) sits oddly beside it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the standard the arbitration clause (c108) and the advancement duty (c096) both operate on, and it must be squared with the covered/uncovered Loss definition (c051).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Arbitration is triggered only 'if requested by the Insured', creating a one-sided and arguably permissive dispute mechanism of the kind courts have had to characterise as mandatory or optional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It covers only allocation of Defense Costs, leaving all other disputes to Section XVI(F) litigation (c117), a division that must be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Subpart (1) treats the Application as a separate application by each Insured Person while subpart (2) denies that the Policy is a series of individual contracts — an internal pull in two directions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be reconciled with the Severability clause (c110) and Severability of Exclusions (c111), which allocate knowledge among Insureds on different terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing sentence — the conditions apply 'whether or not the Insured Person actually knew if the misrepresentation ... was made' — contradicts subpart (1), which forfeits coverage only for a person who knew, and the sentence is itself mangled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It also cuts against the per-person severability promised in Representations (c109)(1) and Severability of Exclusions (c111)(1).
